description: The Caltrans Transportation Equity Index (EQI) is a spatial screening tool from the California Department of Transportation that identifies transportation-based priority populations at census block level. Coverage: all of California, with three screens that each reflect low-income and tribal land status: communities most burdened by the transport system and receiving the fewest benefits, communities with high exposure to traffic and crashes, and communities with the largest gaps in multimodal access to destinations. Caltrans is piloting it in the Caltrans System Investment Strategy and states that it is publicly available for other transport bodies. Format and access: an ArcGIS web map with a how-to guide, EQI v1.0 documentation and responses to comments on the beta. Licence and cost: free to view; no licence is stated. Caveats: unlike CalEnviroScreen (tract level, environmental justice), it uses only transport indicators; download options are not described on the pages read. It can weight investment and capacity planning scenarios towards burdened communities. It relates to the Charlotte Transportation Disadvantage Index and the Caltrans traffic census in the catalogue.
